description: Small Ralph self-iteration focused on restoring main CI health before adding new OSv2-facing capability work. Evidence comes from GitHub Actions run 25996414394 on main after the AI News dogfood merge plus local repository inspection.

userStories.name: Make Go CI build independent of generated WebUI dist
userStories.description: The Go CI job runs `go build ./...` immediately after checkout, before the web job has produced `web/dist` or `cmd/server/web/dist`. `cmd/server/embed.go` currently embeds `all:web/dist`, so fresh checkout builds fail with `pattern all:web/dist: no matching files found`. Remove the compile-time dependency on ignored generated assets while preserving SPA embedding when `make web-build` has populated the dist directory.
bdd_acceptance: Given a fresh checkout with no `web/dist` and no `cmd/server/web/dist`, When `go build ./cmd/server` runs, Then the build succeeds instead of failing on a missing embed pattern.
Given no generated SPA dist is embedded, When the server starts, Then `webDistFS()` returns an error that the existing bootstrap can log as WebUI unavailable while API routes still boot.
Given `make web-build` has produced `cmd/server/web/dist`, When the server binary is built, Then the generated SPA assets remain embedded and `webDistFS()` exposes `index.html`.
Given future edits touch the WebUI embed directive, When targeted tests run, Then they fail if the directive once again points directly at ignored generated `web/dist` output.
ci_evidence: GitHub Actions run 25996414394, Go job Build step: `cmd/server/embed.go:8:12: pattern all:web/dist: no matching files found`.
Repository `.gitignore` ignores both `web/dist/` and `cmd/server/web/dist/`; local dist directories exist only as ignored generated artifacts.
Current `cmd/server/embed.go` uses `//go:embed all:web/dist`, which requires the generated directory to exist at compile time.
quality_gates: Targeted BDD regression test for the embed directive red -> green
Fresh checkout simulation with ignored dist omitted, then `go build ./cmd/server`

userStories.name: Stabilize compliance report downloads in Vitest
userStories.description: The web CI job reaches Vitest and fails in the US-453 ComplianceReportsPage suite with `object.stream is not a function`, leaving SOC2/GDPR download behavior unverified. Make the download test harness and any necessary client code robust across browser Blob implementations and Node/jsdom Blob gaps without weakening the user-facing download assertions.
bdd_acceptance: Given the compliance report endpoint returns a PDF Blob, When the operator clicks Generate & Download in the test browser, Then the captured download has the expected PDF filename/type and no inline `object.stream` error is shown.

Given the GDPR export endpoint returns a ZIP Blob in a Vitest/jsdom environment where Blob streaming is incomplete, When the operator downloads the export, Then the captured ZIP download is recorded once.
Given the API returns a structured 4xx, When the report request fails, Then the inline error shows the backend reason and no download is triggered.
Given `npx vitest run --coverage` runs in CI, When the compliance suite executes, Then US-453 tests do not fail because of Blob stream API differences.
ci_evidence: GitHub Actions run 25996414394, Web job Vitest step: ComplianceReportsPage test rendered `object.stream is not a function` and expected one download but recorded zero.
The failing suite is `web/src/components/admin/__tests__/ComplianceReportsPage.test.tsx`, which mocks response bodies and overrides URL/download behavior.
quality_gates: Targeted BDD/unit regression for ComplianceReportsPage download capture red -> green
`make web-test` or `cd web && npx vitest run --coverage`
